## Observed Facts

- **Data Scope:** BGL dataset, level = FATAL, all time (no start/end filter), all components.
- **855,195 FATAL Log Entries** across **31,481 distinct nodes** [E1].
- **One node dominates:** R30-M0-N9-C:J16-U01 has **152,229 FATAL Log Entries**, about 17.8% of all FATAL Log Entries [E1].
- **Next-highest nodes** have far fewer: R71-M0-N4-C:J14-U01 with 1,567 [E1], R12-M0-N0-C:J12-U01 with 1,385 [E1], and R03-M1-NF-C:J07-U01 with 966 [E1]. The other nodes in the top 50 range from 305 to 966 Log Entries each [E1].
- **By Component:** KERNEL has 626,450 FATAL Log Entries and APP has 228,536 [E2]. LINKCARD has 206 and MMCS has 3 [E2].

## Hypotheses

- FATAL volume is concentrated rather than spread evenly. One node accounts for roughly a sixth of all FATAL Log Entries, so it is the first place to look.
- The many nodes in the 300–400 range in the top 50 share a pattern. They are mostly R00, R02, R03, R22 nodes with `J18` in the name, which suggests a shared rack or card group. This is an inference from node names only, not confirmed by the logs.

## Unknowns

- **How many nodes are truly affected.** The 31,481 figure counts every node with at least one FATAL Log Entry. It does not show how many of those have repeated or recent failures, so the logs alone cannot give a meaningful "affected" count.
- **Whether the volume is recurring or a one-off burst.** I did not measure the time spread. A trend query is needed.
- **Whether the Log Entries are separate incidents.** Log Entries are not incidents, so I cannot say how many incidents produced them.
- **Impact on users or service.** The logs cannot establish this, so I have not assessed it.

## Next Step

Run a trend over time for R30-M0-N9-C:J16-U01 and for the whole FATAL set. That will show whether the top node's volume is a sustained problem or a short spike, and whether the wider FATAL volume is growing.
